title: What is the sum of the first eight odd numbers, found without adding?
description: The video finds the sum of the odd numbers from one to fifteen using the fact that the first few odd numbers add up to a square. Keeko doubts the answer after squaring the last odd number instead of the count of odd numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first n odd numbers add up to n squared, so we count the odd numbers and square the count. Watch for students who square the last odd number instead of the count.

source: Find 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 + 15 without adding term by term.
video_script.why: The child sees that a run of odd numbers from one adds to a square, and that the number being squared is how many odd numbers there are.
video_script.substitution: Count the odd numbers in the sum and square that count.
video_script.anchor: the sum one plus three plus five up to fifteen, with an empty answer box
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko squares the last odd number, fifteen, and says fifteen squared. Fifteen is the last odd number, not how many odd numbers there are; there are eight of them.
maths_rules: the sum of the first n odd numbers is n²: 1 = 1², 1 + 3 = 4 = 2², 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 = 3²
the slip: 15² = 225 squares the last odd number, not the count 8
video_script.design: One idea: n odd numbers from one add to n squared. Wrong idea: squaring the last odd number. The sum stays in the anchor band; the pattern grows on the stage.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the line 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 + 15 in the anchor band with an empty answer box

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: the odd numbers from one to fifteen appear one after another
marks.ask: an empty answer box appears at the end of the line

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Add the odd numbers one, three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen and fifteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the sum, if we do not add term by term?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the empty answer box glows

marks.stop: the empty answer box glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: unit squares grow: 1 is a 1 by 1 square; adding 3 makes a 2 by 2 square; adding 5 makes a 3 by 3 square; each new odd number is an L-shape

marks.three: an L of three unit squares wraps it into a square of side two
marks.five: an L of five unit squares wraps it into a square of side three

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>One unit square is a square of side one.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Add an L of three unit squares and it grows into a square of side two.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Add an L of five and it grows into a square of side three.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the odd numbers from one to fifteen are added.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum, without adding term by term

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum without adding term by term.

marks.count: the odd numbers are counted one by one, from one to eight

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, count the odd numbers. There are eight of them, from one up to fifteen.

beats.on_screen: first n odd numbers add up to n²; n = 8, so the sum is 8²

marks.rule: the rule first n odd numbers add up to n² is written
marks.eight: n is replaced by 8 and the sum becomes 8²

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, the first n odd numbers add up to n squared.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Here n is eight, so the sum is eight squared.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, work out eight squared. It is eight times eight.

marks.pairs: the numbers join in pairs from the two ends, and each pair shows 16
marks.four: the four pairs of 16 are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Step four, check by pairs from the two ends. One and fifteen, three and thirteen, five and eleven, seven and nine all make sixteen.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four pairs of sixteen give sixty four.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is sixty four.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: last number 15, so 15²; the eight odd numbers are counted and 8² replaces it

marks.count: the eight odd numbers are counted under the bubble
marks.fix: 15² is struck and 8² takes its place

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sum is fifteen squared, because fifteen is the last number.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But fifteen is only the last odd number. How many odd numbers there are is a different thing.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>There are eight of them, so eight is the number we square.
